To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ammonium adduct ion of a trimethylsilylated poly(dimethylsilicone) undergoes a specific dissociation process in the gas phase that results in three product ions with a constant relative abundance, regardless of the size and the structure of the precursor ion, and that the dissociation mechanism of the ammonium addducts of the trimethylsilylate end-capped poly(dimethylsilicones) can be explained in terms of the formation of cyclic structures.
the ammonium adduct of a trimethylsilylated poly(dimethylsilane) is a good model to study the fragmentation of large ions and the fragmentation pathways are well understood.

the tandem mass spectrometry of electrospray generated trimethylsilylated poly(dimethylsilane) ammonium adduct ions leads to a very reproducible and predictable behavior and that the dissociation mechanisms are very different from those previously observed in the case of the trimethylsilylation of poly(dimethylsilene).

the study of the fragmentation behavior of electrospray ionized trimethylsilylated poly(dimethylsilicone) ammonium adduct ions.
the study of the dissociation behavior of ammonium adduct ions of trimethylsiloxy-terminated poly(dimethyldimethylsiloxanes) generated by electrospray and submitted to collision-induced dissociation.
the MS/MS of ammonium adduct of PDMS oligomers and the dissociation mechanisms are proposed to account for their fragmentation.
